title: The Capital Stack: Where the Money for Black Business Stops | At The Margins, Ep. 2
lede: Black-founded startups' share of U.S. venture capital fell from 1.5% in 2021 to 0.32% in 2025. Episode 2 of At The Margins goes layer by layer through the capital stack, from family wealth to bank credit, government programs and venture funding, in the U.S. and Canada, and looks at what has measurably moved money to Black-owned businesses.
keyPoints: Black families held 1.4% of the $30.8 trillion in U.S. business equity in 2022; median net worth $44,100 vs $284,310 for white families (Fed SCF, via Urban Institute and the Black Wealth Data Center).

In the Fed's 2025 Small Business Credit Survey, 32% of Black-owned applicants were fully approved vs 57% of white-owned; 32% of Black-owned nonapplicants were discouraged vs 8% (Hope Policy Institute analysis).
SBA backed a record $44.8B in FY2025 with no published race breakdown; MBDA staff were placed on leave in 2025 and the order is in court (GAO); FY2025 CDFI Fund money was held until April 2026.
Black-founded startups raised ~$942M in 2025, 0.32% of U.S. venture (Crunchbase); in Canada, 0.15% (BKR Capital & Rep Matters).
Evidence: fintech lenders made 17.4% of PPP loans but 53.6% of PPP loans to Black-owned firms, and banks that automated roughly doubled their share (Journal of Finance, 2024).
